title: runtime-recover: Wire Runtime::recover to reconstruct RunFrames from journal
description: Feature P0-5. Master §68 (Durable Execution Architecture Contract) requires journal-first recovery: rehydrate slot values, taint, step states from the journal and return them to a caller as a reconstructed RunFrame. Today, vb_runtime/src/runtime/mod.rs:339-362 calls vb_storage::recovery::recover_all_incomplete_runs (recover.rs:274-296), which always returns Summary (no frame data). recover_one_run (line 364-383) drops every Summary. recover_runtime_frame_seed (recover.rs:251-260) is fully implemented but orphaned. insert_into_shard (line 484) passes admission: None. seed.pending_actions is built and dropped. The Runtime is structurally capable of rehydrating, but the wiring is missing. This bead: (1) adds recover_all_incomplete_runs_with_frame_seed to vb_storage::recovery::recover.rs:274+ that calls recover_runtime_frame_seed for each non-terminal run; (2) drops the #[cfg(feature = 'test-util')] gate on Runtime::recover (line 343) and makes it call the new frame-seed function, reattach the RecoveredRunAdmission to RunState.admission, re-attach seed.pending_actions to the shard's action queue, and honor seed.unsupported.action_payloads and seed.unsupported.pending_actions in reject_unsupported_live_frame_state; (3) changes cmd_replay to call Runtime::recover + Runtime::snapshot_run to produce a ReplayReport with reconstructed RunFrame. Acceptance: submit, kill, restart, replay; reconstructed state matches; Kani harness proves bit-identical rehydration; Verus proof per master §68 invariants 1-5.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL reconstruct a complete RunFrame from the journal events alone (slots, taint, step states, admission) without re-executing any step
THE SYSTEM SHALL treat the journal as the ground truth; reconstructed state must equal the live state at the last persisted journal sequence

event_driven.trigger: WHEN the user runs `vb replay <run-id> --db <path>` on a non-terminal run
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL call Runtime::recover, then Runtime::snapshot_run, and emit a ReplayReport containing the reconstructed RunFrame

event_driven.trigger: WHEN the runtime starts and a non-terminal run is detected in the journal
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL call Runtime::recover and re-attach the run to its owning shard with full state

unwanted.condition: IF the journal contains a digest mismatch (workflow, action, or policy)
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT silently default to a substituted value; it must return a typed ReplayDiverged error
unwanted.because: Master §68 invariant 4: recovery is deterministic; divergence is a hard failure

unwanted.condition: IF the journal has a pending action (action scheduled but not yet completed)
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT silently drop the pending action; it must surface it in the run frame's pending_actions list
unwanted.because: Master §68.3: non-idempotent actions are blocked during replay; the operator must decide whether to re-dispatch

preconditions: Run exists in the Fjall journal at the supplied --db path
Run is in a non-terminal state OR terminal with last event RunFinished/RunFailed/RunCancelled
Journal record CRCs verify cleanly (BLAKE3 + CRC32C envelope intact)
postconditions: Reconstructed RunFrame has the same slot values, taint array, and step states as the live frame at the last persisted journal sequence
If pending_actions existed in the live frame, they appear in the reconstructed frame's pending_actions list
If action_payloads existed, they are honored in the gate (master §68.3)
invariants: Rehydration is bit-identical: re-recovering the same journal twice produces two equal RunFrames
Recovery never re-executes a step that has a StepSucceeded journal event
Recovery preserves the digest chain (every event's prev_digest matches the prior event's digest)

happy: runtime_recover_reconstructs_run_frame_from_journal: submit a 5-step workflow, kill the process after step 2, restart, call Runtime::recover; reconstructed RunFrame slots/taint/step_states match the snapshot at step 2
cmd_replay_emits_replay_report_with_reconstructed_frame: `vb replay <id> --db /tmp/db` returns a ReplayReport with a non-empty reconstructed frame
kani_harness_proves_bit_identical_rehydration: 100 random journals, recover twice, assert frame1 == frame2
error: runtime_recover_with_digest_mismatch_returns_replay_diverged: corrupt one byte in the journal; Runtime::recover returns ReplayDiverged
runtime_recover_with_corrupt_crc_returns_io_error: corrupt the CRC32C; Runtime::recover returns IoError with a typed variant
edge: runtime_recover_with_pending_actions_surfaces_them: run a workflow with an action that does not complete; recover; reconstructed frame has pending_actions: [ticket]
runtime_recover_with_unsupported_action_payload_returns_typed_error: a journal entry with an unknown action_id returns UnsupportedActionPayload

patterns: Pattern: existing FjallJournal::recover_full_journal returns Vec<JournalEvent>; we chain recover_runtime_frame_seed on top
Pattern: RecoveredRunAdmission is a struct already in vb_storage/src/recovery.rs; just reattach it
questions: Should Runtime::recover be a method on Runtime or a free function? (Spec: method on Runtime, matches existing structure.)
Does insert_into_shard need a new signature to accept the RecoveredRunAdmission? (Spec: yes; admission parameter is currently None.)

security_failures.failure: An attacker tampers with a journal entry to inject a fake StepSucceeded, causing recovery to skip a step that should have run
security_failures.prevention: BLAKE3 + CRC32C envelope verification; any tampering returns typed IoError, never silent acceptance

usability_failures.failure: Operator sees a successful `vb replay` exit but the reconstructed frame is empty
usability_failures.prevention: ReplayReport includes a `frame.byte_size` field; operator can verify non-zero

data_integrity_failures.failure: Recovery advances pc past a step that the journal says is Waiting (not Succeeded)
data_integrity_failures.prevention: Recovery applies events in strict sequence; no event is applied out of order, and a Waiting step is not marked Succeeded until a StepSucceeded event is seen

integration_failures.failure: Runtime::recover returns a frame but the shard is in a state that cannot accept it (queue full)
integration_failures.prevention: RecoveredRunAdmission is enqueued with priority; shard::tick drains it before any new submissions

Write Verus proof `proof fn recovery_preserves_journal_invariants` in verification/verus/runtime/recovery.rs
phase_2: Phase 5.1 (Storage): Add `recover_all_incomplete_runs_with_frame_seed` to vb_storage::recovery::recover.rs:274+ that calls recover_runtime_frame_seed for each non-terminal run and returns Vec<RunFrameSeed>

Phase 5.2 (Runtime): Drop the #[cfg(feature = 'test-util')] gate on Runtime::recover (line 343); make recover call the new frame-seed function; reattach RecoveredRunAdmission to RunState.admission; re-attach seed.pending_actions to the shard's action queue; honor seed.unsupported.action_payloads and seed.unsupported.pending_actions in reject_unsupported_live_frame_state
Phase 5.3 (CLI): Change cmd_replay in commands/replay.rs to call Runtime::recover + Runtime::snapshot_run and emit ReplayReport with reconstructed RunFrame

phase_4: Run `moon run :test -p vb_runtime -p vb_storage -p vb_cli` and verify all new tests pass
